genZNote: The name literally means 'wheel' — look at it under an electron microscope and you'll see exactly why.

morphology.shape: Double-shelled icosahedral virion with a wheel-like appearance on electron microscopy (the source of its name)

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human gastrointestinal tract, particularly the small intestine
habitat.hostAssociation: Infects and destroys mature enterocytes of the small intestinal villi, impairing absorption

identificationClues: Diagnosed by stool antigen (EIA) testing or RT-PCR, the standard clinical methods
Segmented double-stranded RNA genome with a distinctive double-shelled, wheel-like capsid on electron microscopy
Leading global cause of severe, dehydrating diarrhea in infants and young children
Live attenuated oral vaccines have substantially reduced severe disease and hospitalization where implemented

diseases: Acute gastroenteritis — vomiting followed by watery diarrhea, often with fever, that can progress to severe dehydration in infants and young children
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route, including contaminated hands, surfaces, and objects; highly stable in the environment and resistant to many common disinfectants
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Historically the leading cause of severe diarrheal disease and death in children under 5 worldwide; routine childhood vaccination has dramatically reduced rotavirus-associated hospitalizations and deaths in countries where it has been implemented
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Stool antigen testing (EIA) is rapid and widely available; genotyping/RT-PCR can be used for surveillance and to distinguish wild-type from vaccine strains

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — diagnosed by stool antigen test/RT-PCR
examFacts.importantDisease: Severe dehydrating gastroenteritis in infants — historically the leading cause worldwide
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A segmented dsRNA virus with a distinctive wheel-shaped double capsid, and the leading historical cause of severe infant diarrhea before routine vaccination
